item.title: Squash, golf teams to be elevated to varsity status this summer
item.description: Beginning July 1, Brown's golf and squash teams will be elevated from club to varsity status, according to a recent press release.The men's and women's teams of both sports have been "strong competitors at the club level," which qualified them for this promotion, Vice President for Athletics and Recreation M. item.title: Men's tennis falls 4-3 to Buffalo in first loss of season
item.description: On Sunday morning, the men's tennis team (6-1) came short 4-3 in a home matchup against the University at Buffalo (4-3). Tied 3-3, the deciding singles match saw the Bulls' Theodoros Mitsakos edge past Lukas Phimvongsa '28 in an intense 7-6 (4), 6-4 battle to give Buffalo the victory.Despite the loss overall, the "team played with huge heart against Buffalo," Head Coach Mike Fried '91 wrote in an email to The Herald. "I was incredibly proud of how we competed."Zander Bravo '26 and Ivan Sodan '27

item.title: Fencing upsets Cornell to place sixth out of seven at Ivy Championships
item.description: Over the weekend, women's fencing placed sixth out of seven teams at the Ivy League Fencing Championships, defeating Cornell in a ferocious 14-to-13 upset.The tournament marked a culmination of efforts to "renew" the Brown women's fencing program, Head Coach Charlene Kai Yan Liu told The Herald. item.title: Leggat-Barr '28: Brown should rescue the Superman building
item.description: Rising above the Providence skyline sits a familiar beacon, visible from College Hill night after night: the Superman building. Once one of the nation's most prominent office towers, the skyscraper has sat mostly vacant since Bank of America relocated its headquarters in 2013, 85 years after the building's opening. item.title: Gupta '25 MD'29: True love doesn't have to be romantic
item.description: Every Feb. 14, the world narrows to prix fixe menus, a CVS aisle swathed in pink and the panic of trying to secure a reservation somewhere dimly lit enough.
